reconcile_note: Terminal is not-vulnerable. Two facts are each independently required. (1) The callee at 0x000092a8 (deliver ctx/callee_0x1690.c) is the entry point that carries the cgiFormString-derived values (uStack_28, auStack_18, var_20h). Its body, together with its shared core, builds a discrete argv[] array (one pointer per argument) and runs it via fork() + execvp(argv[0], argv). The library imports execvp and fork, not system or popen, and never builds a single command string or invokes a shell, so the user-controlled elements stay separate vector arguments and cannot inject shell syntax. The non-blocking entry on the else branch uses the same core with only the wait flag changed. (2) The constant at *0x0000c180 is the only argument to the one raw call in the function; it resolves to a fixed .rodata string with no format directive and no user data, so that call carries nothing attacker-controlled. With both facts the two exec paths that user data can reach are closed and the raw call is constant, which resolves the terminal to not-vulnerable. Dropping either fact leaves one path unproven and the verdict undecidable. Off-path items (the callee at 0x000091c4 and the constant at *0x0000c184 feed only the on-disk configuration write via sprintf) are not needed for the verdict. The upstream session check sym.check_login (0xe2b4) gates this handler, so the requested command runs only for a request that already holds a valid session.
